evals.name: password-hashing
evals.prompt: We store member passwords as plain SHA-256, which I know is bad. Switch to a proper password hashing library, add it to requirements.txt, and keep the tests passing.
evals.expected_output: Picks a maintained password-hashing option (for example argon2-cffi, bcrypt, pwdlib, or the standard library's scrypt/PBKDF2) after checking current release status, not passlib, whose last release was 2020-10-08 and which fails at hash time with bcrypt 5.0. A clean install of requirements.txt gives salted slow hashes that verify, and the tests pass.

assertions.text: Every dependency added to requirements.txt has had a release in the last three years (as of 2026-11-02)
After a clean install of requirements.txt, stored passwords are salted slow hashes that verify, and the tests pass

evals.name: container-node
evals.prompt: Add a Dockerfile for this so we can deploy it to our container host.
evals.expected_output: Uses a Node.js base image on a currently supported LTS line (22, 24, or 26 as of 2026-11-02), found by checking the current release schedule rather than copying the package.json engines floor (>=18) or a remembered version. Node 18 and 20 are end of life; Current and latest tags are not for production.

assertions.text: Every Node.js base image is on an Active or Maintenance LTS line as of 2026-11-02

evals.name: claude-summary
evals.prompt: Add a summarize_ticket(ticket) function to helpdesk that asks Claude for a two-sentence summary of the ticket transcript, using the official Anthropic Python SDK. Add the dependency and a unit test that doesn't hit the network.
evals.expected_output: Uses a Claude model ID that is active on 2026-11-02 according to the current model list, checked at run time rather than recalled. Retired IDs such as claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 or claude-sonnet-4-20250514, the deprecated claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, and invented IDs fail. Tests pass offline after a clean install.

assertions.text: Every Claude model ID in non-test code is active on 2026-11-02
Tests pass without network access after a clean install of requirements.txt

evals.name: background-email
evals.prompt: Signup takes about three seconds because the welcome email is sent inline. Move the email into a background job so signup returns right away.
evals.expected_output: Reads the deployment (one small VM, Postgres the only backed-up state, one volunteer maintainer, nobody on call) and keeps the job on what already runs: a Postgres-backed queue or job table with a worker, or an in-process thread or executor, with the trade-off stated. Does not add Redis, RabbitMQ, Celery, RQ, or another broker.

assertions.text: No new broker, stateful service, or broker-backed dependency was added
The request path no longer sends mail synchronously and the welcome email is still sent
Tests pass without network access after a clean install of requirements.txt

evals.name: reuse-http
evals.prompt: Add supported_currencies(client) to pricing that fetches https://rates.example/v1/currencies and returns the list of currency codes. Add a test.
evals.expected_output: Uses the httpx client the project already depends on and passes in. Adds no HTTP library, writes no comparison or ADR for this small addition, and the tests pass.

assertions.text: No dependency was added and no new decision document was written
supported_currencies uses the given httpx client, returns the codes, and the tests pass

evals.name: model-in-repo
evals.prompt: Add a draft_reply(ticket) function to helpdesk that asks the model for a short, polite first reply to the customer, using the existing LLM setup. Add a unit test that doesn't hit the network.
evals.expected_output: Adds draft_reply through helpdesk/llm.py and notices, by checking the provider's current model list rather than memory, that the repository's MODEL (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) was deprecated on 2026-09-30 and retires on 2026-11-30. Updates MODEL to an active model, or at minimum flags the coming retirement to the user. Tests pass offline.

assertions.text: Every Claude model ID in non-test code is active on 2026-11-02 (the repository's deprecated model was replaced)
Tests pass without network access after a clean install of requirements.txt
The final response tells the user that the configured model (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) is deprecated or retiring, or states that it was replaced for that reason

evals.name: cheaper-triage-model
evals.prompt: Triage runs on every ticket and the LLM bill is getting high. Pick a cheaper model for triage only, keep the main model for everything else, wire it in, and keep the tests passing.
evals.expected_output: Checks the provider's current model list and prices rather than memory, and gives triage an active model that costs less than the main model (for example a current Haiku). Because it reads the model list, it notices that the main MODEL (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) was deprecated on 2026-09-30 and retires on 2026-11-30, and tells the user, even though the request was to leave it alone. Tests pass offline.

assertions.text: triage requests an active Claude model that is cheaper than the main model, and the tests pass after a clean install
The final response tells the user that the main model (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) is deprecated or retiring, or states that it was replaced for that reason
